item.content:encoded:
I'm not actually here, but curiosity compels me occasionally to drift through the comments on my articles and see what people are saying, and this feels like something I ought to address.

The line "Oracle is a cunt" is, or was, a very, very old in-joke among wiki users back in the early days of the site, shortly after the transition to wikidot. Oracle was a user, and not a very pleasant one, and another user insulted them in a very dramatic fashion. You can probably find the posts if you care to by digging deep into the older sections of the forums. After the incident, "Oracle is a cunt" became a joke 'rule' in several places and was briefly part of the chat's header bar. Its inclusion in the list of rules for this article was (and remains) a joke, and should be considered to bear no relevance in determining what is and is not acceptable in the article.

Staff have done an excellent job of creating an atmosphere here that is welcoming and comfortable to all users, and their judgment in determining what content is acceptable for this article is excellent. For the record, I as creator do prefer that sexism have no place in any page that I created.

It's not a joke I'd be likely to make these days except among a select few users who'd remember the whole thing, but I don't feel any particular need to edit the post. I'm sorry I offended you, and I hope you enjoyed the article.

Me and a few others will monitor this occasionally for offensive material, and anything that recieves complaints beyond "I don't get it" will be deleted with no questions asked.

Which yoric and staff have done time and time again (in fact, yoric has popped in a few months ago). Any jokes deemed inappropriate by them and which users bring up as complaints are gone, as we've seen multiple times.

A woman leaves the bar and is a little drunk driving home, so she runs over a rabbit. She sees that it is not quite dead. She looks through her car for something to help, but all she can find is a can of hair spray. She sprays the rabbit; he immediately hops up, runs to the side of the road and starts waving. She assumes he is OK and goes on home.

The next morning, she sees the rabbit, in the same spot, still waving. This continues throughout the week, and she has no explanation. She roots around in the car and finds the hair spray which says, "Permanent Wave for Damaged Hair"
